_about: Lookalike patterns for the week of 7 December 2026, read from his Instagram inspo sheet (lookalike-input.json, source sheet): the newest 100 posts plus the sheet's newest 30 carousels, which lookalike.py prepare now adds (the newest 100 rows are the 16 Nov profile-grid backfill and hold no carousel). The sheet captured no slide text for these carousels, so each card_flow is read from each post's caption, summary and page count, never from its slides. Stale sheet: the Instagram inspo sheet's newest row is 2026-11-16, more than 3 days before 2026-11-28; the patterns lean on older posts.

patterns.pattern: A famous name or a big company did a money thing nobody expected, and the post follows the money one fact at a time to a number that makes you stop.
patterns.why_it_travels: A named person or firm plus a surprising number is easy to retell, and the twist (the seller is also paying the bills, the athlete is also the investor) is the bit people forward.
card_flow: The named person or firm and the surprising money move, in one line
What they actually paid or promised, with the number

The biggest single figure
What it adds up to, and the question it leaves

patterns.pattern: A chart, a platform or an awards body just drew a line for AI-made work, and the post explains the old case that forced the rule.
patterns.why_it_travels: Everyone who makes or consumes music, film or art has an opinion on where the line should be, and the trigger story (an AI track 16 weeks in the top 20) is the hook.
card_flow: The new rule, said plainly
What it allows and what it bans
The case that forced it

What it means for the people who make the work

patterns.pattern: A known creator hands part of their channel, voice or face to an AI copy, and the post counts who is watching.
patterns.why_it_travels: It is half joke, half future: a real creator doing the thing people argue about, with a live viewer count as proof.

patterns.why_it_travels: It saves the reader a week of scrolling and lets them pick the one item they want to talk about.

patterns.pattern: A new tool or a limited offer does something creators used to pay for, and the post lists exactly what you get and what it costs.
patterns.why_it_travels: It is useful the same day: the reader saves it to try the offer before it ends.

patterns.pattern: People are using a new model to make games, worlds or art in hours, and the post shows the best three things they made.
patterns.why_it_travels: The examples are visual and slightly unbelievable, and each one invites a 'could I do that'.

patterns.why_it_travels: The AI behaving like a tattletale or a show-off is a story people retell at once; the screenshot is the proof.
